title: Microsoft Purview: Azure PST Import to Exchange Online mailboxes
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's planned workflow and revised rollout windows. The Azure role-assignment path and command are supported, and the licensing and storage costs are appropriately distinguished from unpublished feature-specific requirements.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Azure PST Import to import PST files from Azure Blob Storage directly into Exchange Online mailboxes.
claims.quote: Azure PST Import is a migration method that enables PST files stored in Azure Blob Storage to be imported directly into Exchange Online mailboxes.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a two-step Exchange Migration Service pattern consisting of analysis and migration.
claims.quote: It follows the standard two‑step Exchange Migration Service pattern: an initial analysis phase to validate and assess PST data, followed by execution of the actual migration.

claims.claim: The workflow starts by creating a migration endpoint.
claims.quote: The process also involves creating a migration endpoint

claims.claim: Learn documents an existing PST Import service in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Use the Import service in the Microsoft Purview portal to quickly bulk-import PST files to Exchange Online mailboxes in your organization.

claims.claim: Network upload is one of the documented existing PST import methods.
claims.quote: Network upload: Upload the PST files over the network to a temporary Azure Storage location in the Microsoft cloud.

claims.claim: Drive shipping is another documented existing PST import method.
claims.quote: Drive shipping: Copy the PST files to a BitLocker-encrypted hard drive and then physically ship the drive to Microsoft.

claims.claim: Existing PST import jobs are created on the Import PST files page in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Create a PST import job on the Import PST files page in the Microsoft Purview portal and submit the PST import mapping file you created in the previous step.
